messages:
Raj (support): heads up — getting 4 short P1s from Anya's team: sharp jump in p99 for text-gen API since the canary rollout around 08:10 UTC. Customers see timeouts at ~30s. Escalating.
Maya (runtime): thanks. which canary sha? I saw v2.14.1 go to 10% at 08:05 (sha: 0a1b2c3). Rolling change was 'kernel-selector: prefer-fused-attn' + batching tweak.
Oliver (sre): I'm pulling APM traces now. Quick check: is this widespread or single region? Raj, which region from tickets?
Raj (support): Anya reported eu-west-1 and us-east-1. She pasted two sample request ids: req_eu: rq-9f3a, req_us: rq-4b21. Timeouts show client retry spikes.
Anya (customer): repro steps we used:
1) seq len ~1500 tokens
2) call /v1/generate with model=redwood-small-2026 and temperature=0.2
3) repeated 20x concurrently
We saw p50 ~120ms, p95 ~800ms, p99 ~14s -> timeouts. After rollback we saw p99 back to ~1.2s.
Tessa (perf): sounds like tail for long sequences. Can someone dump latest latency histo for canary vs baseline for seq>1024? I want p50/p95/p99 and qps.
deploy-bot: canary rollout event: v2.14.1 -> 10% traffic at 2026-03-15T08:05:12Z; component=runtime; change=kernel-selector:prefer-fused-attn; batching=enabled(true, target=16)
Maya (runtime): initial metrics: baseline (v2.13.8) p99=1.1s @ seq>1024; canary p99=12.8s. p95 jump is smaller (0.9s -> 1.5s). So tail is huge.
Oliver (sre): grabbing traces...root cause clue: several traces show a single smallish RPC to the GPU host taking 11s, successful but blocking. Could be kernel launch fallback path hitting slow path.
Maya (runtime): kernel-selector change added a fallback when fused-attn kernel fails (we now try fused -> unpacked -> fallback). If fused fails we serialize differently which may trigger big memcopy + syncs. Might explain long single-call latency.
Raj (support): customer says rollback fixed it. Did we already rollback canary to 0%? I don't see an automated rollback.
Maya (runtime): not yet. Plan to throttle canary to 1% and then rollback while we bisect. Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) throttle canary 10% -> 1% 2) block fused-attn flag on canary hosts 3) roll back rollout if tail persists.
Oliver (sre): agree. I'm starting a traffic shift to dedicated fallback pool and redirecting long-seq requests to older runtime via route policy. Command:

```
# shift canary down
redwoodctl rollout set --deployment runtime-canary --percent 1 --reason "p99 tail after kernel selector"
# update routing
redwoodctl route update --match "seq_len>1024" --to runtime-stable
```
Maya (runtime): I'll reproduce locally with the same seed. Share minimal repro script, Anya? Also please dump the GPU host logs for the request ids.
Anya (customer): attached logs in ticket. Also here's a pared-down repro (curl):

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-small-2026","input":"'$(python -c "print('x'*5000)")'","max_tokens":1024}'
```
Tessa (perf): running that now against canary cluster. Observed: host gpu-12 shows a single kernel launch at t=0.28s then a blocking sync at t=11.7s; stackpoints show memmove on fallback path. This smells like fused-attn miscompiled kernel on specific cuda driver combo.
Maya (runtime): which driver? we upgraded some canary hosts to cuda 13.2 last week for perf task. Baseline still on cuda 13.0.
Oliver (sre): bingo. So it's an interaction: kernel-selector picked fused kernel compiled against 13.2, on hosts with 13.0 it falls back to slow path causing long blocking memcopies. Need bisect: is it kernel-selector logic or the host driver mix?
Maya (runtime): two hypotheses:
- H1: kernel-selector's heuristics prefer fused kernel and the fallback path is slow (regression in runtime code)
- H2: the fused kernel binary incompatible with older driver, causing silent fallback and blocking.
Plan: bisect by toggling prefer-fused flag on canary hosts (config) and by forcing host driver version. Also run small A/B: 50% of canary hosts with prefer-fused=false.
Raj (support): customers want ETA. Can we give temporary SLA workaround? We already routed long seq to stable but some traffic still 1% may hit canary.
Maya (runtime): immediate: block fused-attn on canary by env var KERNEL_PREFER_FUSED=false across canary. This is a config-only flip and cheap. If that fails, rollback full canary.
deploy-bot: config update initiated: set KERNEL_PREFER_FUSED=false on runtime-canary group at 2026-03-15T08:45:00Z
Oliver (sre): monitoring charts: within 90s p99 on canary drops from 12.8s -> 1.3s for seq>1024. p95 stable. Errors down. Looks promising.
Tessa (perf): running fleet-level smoke tests across driver variants. So far, when fused disabled, tail disappears on all driver versions. With fused enabled + host cuda13.0 we still see tail.
Maya (runtime): ok summary so far: root cause is combined change: kernel-selector enabling fused-attn caused some hosts with older driver to hit fallback slow path. Mitigation = disable fused-attn by default until we ship compatible kernels or add runtime guard by driver version.
Anya (customer): confirmed on our side: p99 back to acceptable levels. Thanks for the fast response.
Raj (support): marking tickets as mitigated pending postmortem. Customer asked for a timeline for a permanent fix.
Maya (runtime): next steps:
- short term: add preflight check in runtime to query driver version and only enable fused kernels on >=13.2 (assign @Maya) (ETA 1 day)
- medium: rebuild fused-attn binary with backward compatibility or provide fallback optimized path (assign @Tessa, @Maya) (ETA 2 weeks)
- long: expand canary checks to include long-seq p99 synthetic load (assign @Tessa) (ETA 3 days)
Oliver (sre): also add rollout policy to auto-throttle when p99 increases beyond 2x baseline for 3 consecutive mins.
sre-liaison: noted, will add to runbook and open incident for tracking.
Raj (support): final: rollback not needed now, we disabled fused flag and traffic is healthy. I'll close P1s after we confirm stable for 24h. Good job team :thumbsup:
Maya (runtime): thanks everyone. I'll open a short incident writeup and include repro steps, logs, and the config flip commands. We'll also add a canary job for seq>1024 synthetic workload.
Oliver (sre): leaving monitoring alerts on. Ping if we see a regression.
